name: Trussell Trust — Manchester Central Foodbank
eligibility: Anyone in crisis referred by a frontline professional (GP, social worker, university welfare team). Students can obtain a referral voucher from the university wellbeing team.
notes: Simulated data. Contact your university international student support office for a referral voucher. Three-day emergency food parcel provided per visit.

name: University of Manchester — Student Support Fund
eligibility: All registered University of Manchester students experiencing unexpected financial hardship. International students eligible. Evidence of financial difficulty required.
notes: Simulated data. Applications reviewed within 10 working days. Awards are non-repayable grants. Priority given to students at risk of withdrawal.

name: University of Manchester — International Student Advisory Team
eligibility: All international students enrolled at the University of Manchester
notes: Simulated data. Advisors specialise in visa compliance, work rights, and signposting to additional support services.

name: Manchester City Council — Homelessness Prevention Service
eligibility: Anyone at risk of homelessness in Manchester, including international students. Emergency accommodation assessment available.
notes: Simulated data. Out-of-hours emergency number: 0161 234 5001 (simulated). Students should also contact university accommodation office.

name: Greater Manchester Law Centre
eligibility: Low-income individuals and families in Greater Manchester. Free housing, immigration, and employment law advice. No appointment needed for drop-in slots.
notes: Simulated data. Specialist immigration advisers available by appointment. Students facing unlawful eviction or tenancy disputes should contact as early as possible.

name: Student Minds — University of Manchester Chapter
eligibility: All students at Manchester universities. Peer support groups and mental health resources available free of charge.
opening_hours: Drop-in peer support: Wednesdays 14:00–16:00. Online resources available 24/7.
notes: Simulated data. For mental health crises, contact the Samaritans on 116 123 (24/7, free). University counselling service available via self-referral.

name: Trussell Trust — Central London Foodbank (King's Cross)
eligibility: Anyone in crisis with a referral voucher. UCL and other London university welfare teams can issue vouchers to students in need.
notes: Simulated data. Referral vouchers also available via GP surgeries, Citizens Advice, and university student services.

name: University College London — UCL Financial Assistance Fund
eligibility: All registered UCL students in unexpected financial difficulty. International students eligible. Online application with supporting documentation required.
notes: Simulated data. Applications assessed on a rolling basis. Decisions typically within 15 working days. Emergency advances available for urgent cases.

name: UCL — Student Immigration and Visa Advice Service
eligibility: All international students enrolled at UCL
notes: Simulated data. Free OISC-regulated immigration advice. Students concerned about work hour limits or visa compliance should book an appointment.

name: Camden Council — Housing Advice and Homelessness Service
eligibility: Anyone at risk of homelessness in Camden. Students at London universities near the Camden area. Eligibility assessed at first contact.
notes: Simulated data. Students should also contact UCL accommodation office and student union advice centre for specialist student housing support.

name: Shelter England — London Legal Services
eligibility: Anyone facing housing problems in London. Free helpline available to all. Legal representation subject to means and merits test under Legal Aid.
notes: Simulated data. Specialist advice on illegal eviction, deposit disputes, and disrepair. Students with tenancy disputes should call the helpline first.

name: Student Minds — London Hub (UCL/King's/LSE)
eligibility: All students at London universities. Peer support groups run across multiple campuses.
opening_hours: Various campus drop-ins throughout the week. Check website for current schedule.
notes: Simulated data. For mental health crises contact Samaritans on 116 123 (24/7, free) or text SHOUT to 85258.

name: Trussell Trust — Edinburgh Foodbank (Gorgie)
eligibility: Anyone in Edinburgh in crisis with a referral voucher. University of Edinburgh student services team can provide referrals to students.
notes: Simulated data. Additional distribution points across Edinburgh — check the Trussell Trust website for the full list.

name: University of Edinburgh — Student Hardship Fund
eligibility: All registered University of Edinburgh students in financial difficulty. International students eligible. Application via MyEd student portal.
notes: Simulated data. The fund is available year-round. Students are encouraged to apply early as funds are limited. Grants do not need to be repaid.

name: University of Edinburgh — International Student Advisory Service
eligibility: All international students at the University of Edinburgh
opening_hours: Monday–Friday 09:30–16:30, drop-in available Monday and Thursday 10:00–12:00
notes: Simulated data. Advisers hold OISC Level 1 immigration advice accreditation. Can assist with CAS letters, visa extensions, and work rights queries.

name: City of Edinburgh Council — Housing Options and Advice
eligibility: Anyone at risk of homelessness in Edinburgh. Under Scottish law, all homeless applicants are entitled to a full homelessness assessment.
notes: Simulated data. Scottish housing law offers stronger protections than England and Wales. Students in Edinburgh should also contact the university accommodation emergency line.

name: Citizens Advice Edinburgh — Housing and Immigration Legal Advice
eligibility: Anyone in Edinburgh regardless of immigration status. Free, confidential, and impartial advice.
opening_hours: Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00. Drop-in available Monday and Wednesday 09:00–12:00.
notes: Simulated data. Advisers can help with tenancy disputes, deposit issues, and signpost to Scottish Legal Aid Board for funded legal representation.

name: Student Minds — University of Edinburgh Chapter
eligibility: All students at Edinburgh universities. Peer support available free of charge.
opening_hours: Weekly peer support group: Tuesdays 13:00–15:00. Online resources available 24/7.
notes: Simulated data. For mental health crises in Scotland call Breathing Space on 0800 83 85 87 (free, Monday–Thursday 18:00–02:00, Friday 18:00–Monday 06:00). Samaritans 116 123 available 24/7.
